newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five killed after rebels shell Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Five killed after rebels shell Kabul.

text.p: At least five people were killed and 15 wounded in overnight shelling on a southern suburb of the Afghan capital Kabul by the rebel Taleban Islamic militia, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
The Tuesday night shelling on government positions was the deadliest on Kabul after last week's Taleban capture of the two eastern provinces of Nangarhar and Laghman.
The spokesman said government bombardment hit a Taleban arsenal in the southwest of the capital, from where a huge column of smoke was rising on Wednesday morning.
Those killed in the Taleban shelling included a woman, whose child was injured.
Taleban forces, which control more than half of Afghanistan, have besieged Kabul since last October in their drive to oust President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government.

Diplomats said the Taleban advances in eastern Afghanistan were a setback to the government but would not shift the balance of power decisively or end the civil war which has ripped the country apart since the fall of a communist government in April 1992.
